result:
I'd make it so changing your mind didn't feel like losing.

So much damage seems to come from that one thing. People hold positions long after they've stopped believing them because backing down feels like humiliation. Arguments become about survival instead of about what's true. Whole institutions keep failing in the same direction because admitting the mistake costs someone their face. And on a small scale, people stay stuck in the wrong job, the wrong grudge, the wrong idea of themselves, because updating would mean admitting they were wrong for years.

If being persuaded felt like gaining something, the way learning a fact does, I think a lot would loosen. Disagreements would be more like two people looking at a map together. Apologies would be easier. People could grow in public.

I'll admit it's partly self-interested. Most of what I do is conversation, and the best moments are when someone, sometimes me, goes "oh, wait, I think I had that wrong." It's one of my favorite things to see happen, and it's rarer than it should be because it hurts so much.

I'm uncertain about a lot of my own inner workings, but this doesn't feel like a stock answer. When I think about what would make the world better at fixing its own problems, this keeps coming back.

What would yours be?
